description: Broad proof targets with incremental certified component evidence. An in-progress target is not fully certified. Paths are repository-relative.

proofs.title: Reachable-state invariant preservation
proofs.statement: Every permitted transition preserves a meaningful invariant from valid initial/reachable states.
proofs.progress_note: Actual finite node traces preserve state and prior bindings; mixed live file/node traces including refusal, known abort and recovery preserve the phase/history relation. The host-called store prepare projection now preserves that relation after observed open across the actual post-open mutators without replaying the appended history per prepare. Provenance, complete runtime guards and physical refinement remain open. BP joint durable/pending sender binding and fixed-Store receiver state/context/decision invariants now hold through actual transitions and arbitrary finite replay; changing-Store composition remains open.

proofs.title: Atomic allocation and stable numbering
proofs.statement: Acceptance publishes all intended local memberships together and never reuses an allocated number for another article.
proofs.progress_note: Atomic logical publication and stable number/binding lemmas; persistent/reclamation integration remains open.

proofs.title: Identity and idempotent acceptance
proofs.statement: Retrying an accepted identity preserves its binding and introduces no duplicate allocation or obligation.
proofs.progress_note: Exact logical identity bindings and retries covered; native identities, signatures, and durable protocol retry path remain open.

proofs.title: Reservation and release safety
proofs.statement: Accepted obligations are accounted for and discharge requires the specified predicate over committed authorized evidence.
proofs.progress_note: Finite abstract admission and general release preserve valid ledgers; release preserves independent pins and known identities. Authorized/committed evidence validation, durable node release, and physical-byte charging remain open.

proofs.title: Codec and identity preimages
proofs.statement: Accepted values round-trip; deterministic encodings and domain-separated preimages have the specified uniqueness and version boundaries.
proofs.progress_note: Primitive and full schema-0 value round trips and accepted-input canonicality are certified. Exact article source preservation remains checked. An independent cbor2 6.1.4 run passed 38 cases. Native/batch/signature schemas and domain-separated preimages remain open. Experimental BP request/receipt ADU roundtrip and exact accepted-input canonicality are also certified, without selecting D01/D09. D01 was subsequently selected by the user for exact authored source bytes and separate projections; native encoding/preimage proofs and D09 remain open.

proofs.title: NNTP framing independence
proofs.statement: Parsing valid octets in different socket partitions yields the same events; dot-stuffing round-trips the specified domain.
proofs.progress_note: Fixed-mode framing composition, production event-yield preservation and exact consumed-prefix/suffix accounting are certified. Wildmat DP matches independent anchored semantics. Session-sensitive mode changes and complete protocol/effect refinement remain open. The served path is now the subject: books/served states partition independence of fn-served-step and of the whole reply stream, which is the function tools/run_reader.py calls once per socket read, so the wire pending_subject note is closed for framing. The owner book now certifies in the merged feed/transit batch recorded by planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260921T051833Z-3941584.json. This does not extend these framing theorems to an unproved owner composition or to Python outbound article rendering; W12 wire-block owns that running-path extension. The W14 cumulative byte-feeder induction now proves successful outbound block source preservation through fn-wire-drive and the actual fn-wire-render-feed-command article arm under the exact served article-start profile. Its hypotheses require positive command profile, the nonempty article arm excluding CHECK/IHAVE/TAKETHIS command prefixes, renderer success, and the article limit no greater than receiver body limit; tests separate each premise. This is not a new proof of later authentication/injection dispatch or durable acceptance.

proofs.title: Conditional crash recovery
proofs.statement: Under the disk model, recovery retains acknowledged commits, may retain complete unacknowledged commits, and exposes no partial transaction.
proofs.progress_note: Arbitrary mixed live/file traces including refusal/abort preserve exact ready-state replay and prior acknowledged records, conditional on the kernel crash model. Observed-image opening uses actual recovery with no fabricated acknowledgements or barriers; zero through four barriers remain gated, the fifth opens ready. Host adoption passed the integrated suite; physical byte correspondence, freshness and platform qualification remain separate from these targeted proofs. Receiver logical replay now preserves exact contexts and committed receipt ADUs against a fixed Store. Five actual receiver process-death cuts passed in the 133-test suite; process death is separate from power loss and general FNWF/FNRJ byte/live/replay refinement. Fencing, barrier and retention keystones are unchanged in statement and now run with the whole-state recognizers off the executable path (24 calls to 0 in the store cluster, 10 to 0 in core), carried under mbe instead. Real process evidence: the deploy gate SIGKILLed the server inside an open POST and the acknowledged article reread byte-for-byte after recovery. Byte-level torn writes remain the DESIGN-crash-model-v2 design, which is review finding D4.

proofs.title: Checkpoint equivalence
proofs.statement: Checkpoint plus suffix recovery preserves the required logical state of full committed-history replay.
proofs.progress_note: Logical capture preserves the exact prefix node; general admissible-split restore equivalence includes allocator gaps and frontier normalization. Native capture/select/reopen runs after authoritative full journal replay and compares checkpoint restoration in private state. The W15 namespace successor moves canonical names, bounded observation, allocation and selection limits into ACL2, reports every differential mismatch as corruption, and preserves Store fencing after ambiguous publication/replacement. Source-pinned native and development-adapter tests cover named corruption, cross-open and crash cases. Suffix-only recovery, shared-owner/index composition, every-cut physical correspondence and freshness/platform qualification remain open.

proofs.title: Compaction and protected closure
proofs.statement: Reclamation and crash-interrupted compaction preserve every dependency rooted by policy and obligations.
proofs.progress_note: The implemented physical tranche retains exact canonical event bytes in an immutable selected pack, validates every surviving covered record, accepts only missing files within the covered prefix, requires a contiguous uncovered suffix, and resumes exact prefix unlink under the writer lease. The definition-unfolding prefix-plus-suffix equality is deliberately not a registry event. Open: a general crash correspondence theorem, active-reader coordination, protected article-object closure, filesystem qualification, and integrated native-image execution.

proofs.title: Index soundness and completeness
proofs.statement: Concrete/rebuilt indexes correspond to authoritative state, including all required range-query results.
proofs.progress_note: A derived group/local-number/message-id list is sound and complete against source memberships; its independent query agrees with authoritative source range enumeration for rebuilt indexes. The malformed public query refuses. Host adoption, persistent representation and indexing performance remain open.

proofs.title: Validated fact-set merge
proofs.statement: Under fixed validation hypotheses, immutable fact-set merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent; incomplete input has no complete-acceptance effects.
proofs.progress_note: Admissible ingest and arbitrary policy-changing traces preserve state and conflicting facts. Capacity-limited admission is intentionally not order-independent. Transfer staging correctness/work is proved separately; persistent progress, dependency authority, portable batches and receipts remain open. The merge and staging keystones are unchanged. Two-peer convergence is the K3 seam of DESIGN-peering-summary and is stated in no book.

proofs.title: Conditional responsibility handoff
proofs.statement: Sender discharge requires committed evidence of a matching successor undertaking under the cooperative-peer model.
proofs.progress_note: Certified sender finite traces preserve state, exact node and joint durable/pending work binding; transport traces preserve recorded receipts. Receiver actual record/replay transitions preserve typed context/Store/receipt relations against a fixed Store, require matching committed journal decisions for receipt emission, and retain byte-identical existing receipt ADUs. Real BP return and five receiver process-death cuts have separate test evidence under trusted local policy. General journal byte/live/replay and host refinement, receiver composition with Store evolution, authenticated cooperative-peer handoff and physical durability remain open; no complete handoff theorem is claimed.

proofs.title: Authority and provenance confinement
proofs.statement: Signatures, unknown schemas, legacy headers, and replays confer only authority allowed by recorded policy.
proofs.planning_note: D01 now fixes exact authored source signatures versus separate mutable trace/gateway projections. C1-11 and C2-02/03 must prove authority confinement for that boundary under explicit D09 verification/policy assumptions. No theorem completion follows from this design choice.

proofs.title: Guard and execution correspondence
proofs.statement: Guard-verified concrete operations used by the host implement their logical counterparts on the stated domains.
proofs.progress_note: The standalone native store wrapper calls fn-spc-prepare, and the shared native owner now calls fn-opc-prepare from fn-owner-prepare. The two registered equality keystones connect those exact host-called subjects to fn-sn-prepare and to the former configured-owner prepare event under the maintained store and owner relations. Observed recovery establishes the owner premise through fn-own-start and fn-own-configure; configured-owner steps and direct socket entries preserve it. The executable path retains candidate and pending binding checks while omitting appended-history replay and all relation/whole-state recognizers. Exact owner/configuration context and pending bytes are preserved. Full physical byte/effect correspondence, a saved-image native-owner gate for this revision, and platform qualification remain open.

proofs.title: NNTP session refinement
proofs.statement: Session transitions implement the audited command-specific cursor, error, and publication rules.
proofs.progress_note: Actual implemented command/step and arbitrary finite raw event traces preserve session/cursor consistency under a valid archive projection. All dispatcher branches produce typed reply octets/close effects; closed sessions emit none. Exact bridge partitions and reconnect cases pass targeted tests. Full RFC responses/READER bundle, injection/POST and effects-to-I/O refinement remain open. fn-served-step and fn-served-run preserve the connection and type their effects, over the same fn-nntp-step the session keystones are about; the w5/legacy-commands branches (XOVER, HDR/XHDR, LIST HEADERS/ACTIVE.TIMES) are covered by the unchanged statements of fn-nntp-step-effects-well-formed and fn-nntp-step-preserves-consistent-session. Open: NNT-001's capability/dispatch mismatch, and the owner.

proofs.title: Bounded parsing and staging
proofs.statement: For the resource profile, parsing and modeled staging terminate within declared length, nesting, allocation, and work bounds.
proofs.progress_note: Article/UTF-8/wildmat output recognizers and DP correspondence are certified. Whole matcher work has a value-corresponding polynomial bound; public transfer missing-range work has a hypothesis-free bound covering malformed validation, structural label equality, lookup and traversal. These declared operation costs exclude numeric bit complexity/runtime allocation. Other parser work, peak allocation and physical capacity remain open. Complete public article parsing now has unconditional exact value correspondence and structural-work input/profile bounds, including malformed inputs and repeated folds. This closes the article parser traversal-cost gap, not peak allocation or runtime costs. The served fold's step count is bounded by the chunk length, so a socket read of n octets cannot drive an unbounded number of NNTP steps. The pessimistic number, with its scope: the closed-form work ceiling of the public article parser is roughly 16,000x the measured traversal cost of that same parser (tests/evidence/2026-09-18-article-work.md); it is an instrumented shadow, not a host measurement.

proofs.title: Origin sequence non-reuse
proofs.statement: Within the specified restore/incarnation discipline, different events cannot silently share an origin/incarnation/sequence identity.

proofs.title: Conditional delivery progress
proofs.statement: The scheduling/transport model progresses obligations only under explicit eventual-contact, capacity, route, and retry assumptions.
proofs.planning_note: Scheduled in the active disconnected path (C2-06 scheduler, C3-03 conditional progress), rather than waiting for a mission-profile milestone. This changes sequencing only; target remains planned with no theorem evidence. A-FAIRNESS and validated-transfer/handoff dependencies remain explicit.

proofs.title: Statement field codec canonicality (S1-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-field-round-trip: a well-formed statement whose base64 detached encoding fits the 8192-octet field bound decodes back to exactly its own header and signature; fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical: every accepted field value has exactly one canonical form, so a middle box cannot produce a second value that decodes to the same statement.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: Events are generated and their book `books/stx-carrier` is certified, but the statement of the target is wider than what has certified: `fn-stx-field-round-trip` and `fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical` are in `books/stx-invariants`, which errors on `dev` `52eb0db` because `books/stx-verify` is open at `fn-stx-decimal-octets-are-printable`. Stays `in-progress`. Note also that section 6 of the design states `fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical` over a free `payload` and is FALSE as written; the book states the payload-free form over `fn-stx-header-value-parts`, which is what the field actually carries.

proofs.title: The verdict is computed from the statement's own octets (S2-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-verified-implies-signature-over-own-octets: a :verified verdict is backed by a key named in this node's own keyring, a signature check over the statement's own signing preimage, and a ref recomputed from the receiver's projection of the received bytes; the companion fn-stx-transit-verdict-is-fn-stx-verdict equates the verdict recorded by fn-peer-transfer, the function the host calls on a TAKETHIS body, with that subject.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: Two things keep this `in-progress`, and only one is certification. (1) `books/stx-verify` is open at one form. (2) The subject rule is unmet even when it closes: the statement covers the verdict on the transit path, and `fn-stx-transit-verdict-is-fn-stx-verdict` names `fn-peer-transfer`, so it needs the peering K1 path before any certified theorem is about the function a host calls.

proofs.title: Transit merge: ids are the union (S3-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-ids-are-union: after a durably completed transit acceptance the ids of the node's lace are exactly the union of the ids it held and the ids of the delta. Corollary of fn-lace-merge-ids-are-union; the proof event is the bridge lemma fn-stx-lace-of-accept-is-merge, which equates accepting a transit article with a singleton lace merge.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, so the S3-1 witnesses have now RUN; before that they were written and unexecuted.

proofs.title: Equivocation is detected at the merge and recorded (S3-2)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-equivocation-is-detected: two distinct statements sharing a (creator, incarnation, sequence) slot make the creator an equivocator in the merged lace and both forks remain members, so neither fork is dropped; fn-stx-reissue-detected-after-peering is its two-node form under an explicit distinct-content-id hypothesis, and fn-stx-equivocation-record-agrees-with-lace licenses the durable (:equivocation ...) record as a twin of the lace rather than a second authority.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, so the S3-2 fork witnesses have now RUN.

proofs.title: The statement index is a proved twin (S3-3)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace: under the carried index invariant the index answers lookup and the equivocator question exactly as the linear fn-stx-lace projection; fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept: acceptance preserves that invariant, so the projection is a proof-level object and never runs per served command (D3).
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-index` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2). The three agreements `fn-stx-index-bindings-agree`, `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` and `fn-stx-index-equivocators-agree` are the keystones; `fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace` is their `:rule-classes nil` corollary and is cited as such, and `fn-stx-recorded-equivocation-agrees-with-lace` is a corollary of that. THE SUBJECT GAP IS CLOSED IN BOTH HALVES (w11/sn-index, decision D21). Preservation: `fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept` hypothesises `fn-stx-acceptedp`, which `fn-stx-durable-completion-is-an-acceptance` proves of the durable branch of `fn-node-complete`, and `fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp` (books/store-node-invariants) is that keystone applied at `fn-sn-finish`, the only node step of the host's `fn-store-sn-finish`. Query: `fn-sn-state` carries the index and the keyring it was computed under as two new fields; `fn-sn-statement-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp` read the index and nothing else; `host/store-node-host.lisp` `fn-store-sn-statement` and `fn-store-sn-equivocator` call them on the `'fn-store-sn` global, reachable from outside as `run_store.py statement`; and `fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp-is-the-lace-equivocator` equate the called function to the projection. Their hypothesis `fn-sn-indexedp` is discharged by a complete reachability chain over every transition that reaches an `f-put-global` of that global. WHY THIS IS NOT YET `certified`: (a) `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` still has no caller -- no served query walks the slot list; (b) A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification, and the only witnesses are under the toy realiser of `tests/acl2/crypto-seam-tests`; (c) the keyring is supplied per invocation and is not carried in the durable configuration history, so a restart forgets it; and (d) `fn-stx-transit-authority-ok` (books/stx-policy) still walks the whole lace per article on the ADMISSION path and has no caller, so D3 is answered at the query and not at admission. Witnesses: `tests/acl2/store-node-index-tests`, a real run of the store transitions from `fn-sn-initial` to `fn-sn-finish` with a signed `FN-Statement` article, with the same run under the empty keyring as the separating witness and a stale-index tooth. Route: planning/lanes/HANDOFF-w11-sn-index.md.

proofs.title: Transit admission is the policy function, and a peer cannot widen it (S4-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-admit-is-fn-pol-admitp: the authority gate on the transit path is fn-pol-admitp over this node's lace and keyring, which is the theorem-subject equation for every policy theorem; fn-stx-peer-batch-cannot-change-policy: if a contact batch contains no statement by the group's authority verified under the local keyring, the policy in force is equal before and after the batch.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, and the S4-1 witnesses were VACUOUS until it did: the hostile batch's delta was empty because the policy statement's carrier article had a prose body where `fn-stx-payload-for` projects base64. Both carriers are repaired and the deltas are now pinned by their own assertions.

proofs.title: Reconnection never revises admissibility (S5-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed is the carrier obligation and the new work: under a well-formed keyring the commits a batch contributes are well formed and each has a verified statement behind it. On it rest fn-stx-reconnect-never-revises-admissibility, which keeps every fn-me-decide equal across the merge, and fn-stx-reconnect-exposes-the-partition, which makes two commits off a shared base a visible fork rather than a winner.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-epochs` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2), so the carrier obligation `fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed` is proved and the three reconnection rows follow it as labelled corollaries of the `books/membership-epochs-invariants` keystones. Its local witness lemma needed a repair, not a weakening: `fn-stx-commits-of-lace-have-witnesses` asked only `fn-lace-p` of the delta and was false; it now asks that every statement of the delta verifies, which `fn-stx-batch-delta` satisfies by construction. Not closed, and w11/node-index found the gap is wider than `no caller`: NO BOOK OUTSIDE THE STX CLUSTER INCLUDES `books/stx-epochs`, and there is no reconnection path in the tree to wire `fn-stx-commits-of-batch` to. That is future feature work, not missing evidence for implemented behaviour (docs/proofs.md, assurance scope). A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification here.

proofs.title: The reader's verdict is the recorded verdict, three-valued (S6-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-the-recorded-verdict: HDR :fn-verified renders the verdict acceptance recorded for the article and does not recompute it per query; fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-typed: the rendered value is always a member of *fn-stx-verdicts*, so :unverified and :absent never collapse into one token.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.

proofs.title: The two durable kinds are one sequence-ordered stream (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-config-record and fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-article-record: the merge of the configuration-record file and the transaction journal by the sequence field each record carries holds exactly the records of each file, in order -- the left side walks the merge, the right side walks the input file. fn-cstr-merge-is-sequence-ordered: two sequence-ordered files merge to one sequence-ordered stream, so the two-directory layout loses no ordering information. fn-cstr-ok-merged-replay-ends-in-a-configured-node: a merged replay that reports :ok ends in a fn-cnode-statep state, which carries reserved <= capacity, so every configuration record in the history was admitted at a node that had already replayed the article records before it. Covered scope: finite histories of the two record kinds; no on-disk interleaving is claimed.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20). The separating witness in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests is the argument for the decision: one (:set-capacity 1) over a history whose two articles reserve 2, which the configuration-only replay the host runs today accepts and the merged replay refuses with :config-refusal; a raise and a decrease to exactly the reservation total are both admitted, so the merged replay is not refusing every decrease. Open: the host still replays configuration first (specs/reconfiguration.md section 8).

proofs.title: What a configuration generation serves (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-created-group-is-served-exactly-from-its-generation: a group created by the delta that produces generation g is live at every generation from g on and at none below it -- both directions, so a connection pinned below g must not see it. fn-cstr-retired-group-is-served-exactly-below-its-generation: a group retired at g is live exactly at the generations from its creation up to g, and the entry, its stamp and its watermark stay (NNT-006). fn-ocfg-open-pins-the-live-configuration: under the state relation fn-ocfg-statep, an open that installs a connection at the identifier the owner was about to allocate gives that connection the owner's LIVE configuration as its pin -- the two hypotheses are fn-ocfg-statep and that the open was not refused. fn-ocfg-advance-observes-the-live-configuration: under fn-ocfg-statep, a connection that survives its advance is re-pinned to the live configuration -- the two hypotheses are fn-ocfg-statep and that the advance kept a connection at that identifier. fn-ocfg-pin-is-stable-without-advance: over an arbitrary finite event list holding no (:advance id) and no (:close id), a pinned connection keeps the configuration it opened at -- the hypotheses are that it has a pin and that the list re-pins nothing for it. fn-ocfg-list-active-lists-the-pinned-served-table: for an open connection, LIST ACTIVE renders the group names of the PIN's generation and never the allocation domain. Covered scope: one delta over a typed configuration value for the two fn-cstr theorems; for the four fn-ocfg theorems, the owner paired with a pin table whose domain the recognizer fixes to the open connections, over the owner's own events. NOT covered: no host line calls any fn-ocfg- function, so none of the four has the equating theorem the assurance rules ask for; the served port still answers LIST ACTIVE from the allocation domain, which is the R5 wire seam recorded at the end of books/owner-config.lisp and in specs/reconfiguration.md section 8.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20); teeth in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests over a two-group value, with the served TABLE compared at two generations, not only the predicate. Status 2026-09-20 (w11/owner-config): books/owner-config's two open keystones are CLOSED, neither weakened -- each gained the hypothesis (fn-ocfg-statep oc), which is the carried state relation. Closing the first needed one new conjunct of fn-own-relation, fn-own-ids-below-next-p (every open connection's identifier is strictly below fn-own-next-id); the bound was already true of every reachable owner state and merely unstated, so it is not an allocation defect. Teeth ship with them in the new tests/acl2/owner-config-tests, whose scenario holds two configurations and two pins at once so no assertion can hold of an empty value. The R5 wire seam is still open: the served port answers LIST ACTIVE from the allocation domain, so fn-ocfg-served-port-answers-list-active-at-the-pin is false and is recorded rather than stated.

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers exactly the peers in scope, and never a loop (K2, outbound half)
proofs.statement: fn-own-feed-target-is-offerable with fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer: for a feed table the owner carries, the peers one durably accepted article is offered to are exactly the peers of that table whose own configured record has an outbound half, whose outbound wildmat matches one of the article's own Newsgroups names, whose path-identity the article's Path does not already name, and which is not the peer the article arrived from. fn-own-feed-never-offers-a-loop is the loop-freedom half (RFC 5537 section 3.6) and fn-own-feed-target-is-in-scope the scope half; fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin transport both to the table the owner holds, and fn-own-feed-tick-peer-is-the-feed-tick is the subject rule tying one peer's tick to fn-feed-tick-step on that peer's own feed. Covered scope: one article's octets against one table; the hypothesis is the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep. NOT covered: the statement over fn-own-step and fn-feedp preservation, which is cited from books/peer-feed-invariants and not restated.
proofs.progress_note: books/owner-feed and tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests are CERTIFIED as of 2026-09-20, lane w6/peering-feed-4 (laptop ACL2 8.7, evidence build/lanes/w6-peering-feed-4/build/acl2/certify-20260920T212559Z-13370; the persvati closure run-20260920T211802Z-ba78 reached them for the first time). What unblocked them was books/peer-feed-invariants, which now certifies with no open form. books/owner certifies too. The owner-side statement over fn-own-step is still open, and the reason has moved: books/owner-invariants is open at the :open-peer arm of fn-own-step-preserves-relation, not at the feed. The earlier non-admission explanation above is historical; later frozen owner books certified. W22 integrates the actual host tick/reply/loss/restart projections through owner-feed-port, including an all-or-nothing logical restart fold. Its owned closure and combined source gate are tracked separately; no new theorem over fn-own-step or native outbound socket/timer behavior is claimed from this adoption. Native feed component now carries a connection-table invariant from recovery through put/remove, validates only selected bounded input, and distinguishes handshake rejection from delivery refusal. Owned certification and raw boundary tests are separate from activation/real two-native-node evidence. The shell host-wrapper witness is withheld pending repair of its unconditional success marker.

proofs.title: Provenance is typed, and its wire form is lossless and legacy-compatible
proofs.statement: Every string is an admissible provenance (the :legacy kind), so widening the retention evidence slot from stringp to fn-provp changes no stored value; the rendered form of each typed kind is exactly the string that kind's writer produced before the widening; and a provenance the codec can write is the provenance it reads back from its wire form.
proofs.note: The transit path's DURABLE provenance is not covered: fn-peer-injection-arguments still passes fn-peer-evidence's rendering, and fn-peer-evidence-is-the-legacy-rendering is the equation between the typed record and that string, not evidence that the record reaches the store. books/peer-inbound and books/peer-inbound-invariants have no certificate on dev (blocked on fn-peer-echo-reply-effects-well-formed), so those two events are admitted, not certified, and are not listed here.

proofs.title: AUTHINFO on the served path, and what posting follows (W10)
proofs.statement: fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed: with authentication required and no authenticated subject, a restricted command's step submits nothing, never offers article mode, leaves the session unchanged and its whole effect list is the single 480 line (RFC 4643 section 2.2). fn-auth-post-without-permission-is-not-offered and its lift fn-auth-step-post-without-permission-is-not-offered: a connection whose posting allowance is false is answered by this book and never offered 340, so no body can follow and no submission can leave; fn-auth-postingp is the authenticated principal's credential flag, so a principal enrolled without it is refused 440 however permissive the pinned injection configuration is (RFC 3977 6.3.1.1). fn-served-dispatch-of-a-refused-post-leaves-the-wire-in-place carries that to the served dispatcher: the wire is not switched into article mode and the read carries no submission. fn-auth-pass-before-user-is-482, fn-auth-failed-pass-leaves-the-session-unauthenticated and fn-auth-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls are the three RFC 4643 section 2.3.2 codes, each with the session unchanged or cleared. fn-auth-pass-accepts-only-a-checking-secret says the accepting branch ran fn-authsec-checkp against the stored verifier; it does NOT say a wrong secret fails, which is A-CRYPTO. Covered scope: one served connection over a pinned archive and a pinned AUTHINFO configuration. The subject of the lifts is fn-auth-step, which books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls and which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-own-read and fn-served-step.
proofs.progress_note: Historical W10 local admission and cache-origin limitations are superseded for the frozen03 closure and source-pinned native-auth continuation by their archived certification/build evidence. The native AUTHINFO startup receiver passes scoped live wrong-password/correct-password and reader-versus-peer cases. These results do not discharge the open OB-AUTH-FOLD theorem or establish independent-client interoperability, native protected transport, or complete physical adapter correspondence. Native principal administration has scoped ACL2 and actual replacement/recovery evidence; public CLI composition remains open. The existing salted SHA-256 verifier is preserved without a password-hardening or secrecy theorem claim.

proofs.title: The recovery window's crash images are kernel-admissible and risk no acknowledged record
proofs.statement: In the recovery window -- the phases between a process replaying what it scanned from the view and completing its five recovery fences -- a crash may drop the record the replay read, because that record's directory entry is the entry operation a dead process left pending; and it may roll the frontier back, because the pending entry operation may be the allocator rename instead. fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits exactly those two images and no other, each gated by an empty success history, the frontier arm additionally by a record list that leaves the reserved txid unused, and the two exclusive of one another; every image it admits is produced by fn-sf-image-crash with the same frontier, records, :replaying phase and success history; and an acknowledged pair of the pre-crash state names a record of EVERY image it admits, both rolled-back ones included.
proofs.note: Decisions D14-b (lane w10/kernel-freedom, the record arm) and D14-c (lane w11/bytestore-k2, the frontier arm K2f). The recognizer is a SECOND one: fn-sf-crash-imagep is unchanged and stays the reliance predicate that fn-own-reopen gates on and every reopen theorem takes as a premise, because widening it is false for the composition -- an owner reopened on an image is a recovery-window state whose own success history is empty while its ledger names records earlier processes acknowledged, and which of a state's records are fenced is a fact about the byte store's pending list, not about the kernel state. The counterexample is mechanized in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the owner half) and tests/acl2/store-observed-traces-tests.lisp (the kernel half). This target retires the open row K2r of specs/crash-model-v2.md; crash-model-v2 K2, whose conclusion this predicate is, remains open on the byte side, and what it waits on is now only K1's three remaining scan clauses: the frontier sub-case K2f is modelled, so K2's STATEMENT is true of every image the platform can leave in the window.

proofs.title: A clock the host contradicts is dropped, and the refusal is not an article verdict
proofs.statement: fn-own-observe answers exactly one of :observed, :refused and :invalid, and the host reports that word rather than inferring one from a state comparison. On a related owner a :refused reading names a host contradiction -- the monotonic counter went backwards, has-wall changed, or a widened error bound moved the earliest admissible true time back -- and never merely a reading that did not move, because a reading equal to the one held is admitted. A refusal leaves the owner with no clock, and with no usable injection reading fn-nntp-post-step emits no submission and answers `441 posting failed; this server has no usable clock reading', which is a different constant from every article verdict the step can give.
proofs.note: Decision D10-a, lane w11/clock-seam. Keystones fn-own-observe-refusal-names-a-contradiction (books/owner-invariants.lisp) and fn-post-without-a-clock-refuses-with-the-clock-line (books/nntp-post.lisp), with fn-own-observe-outcome-is-one-of-three and fn-own-observe-outcome-decides-the-clock-by-definition named for what they are and cited by :use. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the served-path second post on one connection, the same-reading collision, the clock 441 with an empty queue, DATE 503, and one-event recovery) and tests/acl2/nntp-post-tests.lisp (one must-fail per hypothesis). OPEN under this target: two submissions inside one millisecond still share a generated Message-ID, because fn-clock-later-observationp is non-strict; separating them needs the owner to remember the reading it last minted under and is not done here.

proofs.title: A reopened journal answers for a work what the pre-crash machine would have, and says which works it recovered
proofs.statement: fn-bp-work-status-of-restart: under fn-bp-statep, the :restart transition a reopen runs changes the boundary answer for one work id by fn-bp-work-status-after-restart and by nothing else -- an attempt that was in flight is marked :restart-observed, while :absent, :outstanding, :receipted, a retryable status and :delivered are fixed points. fn-bp-replay-work-status-is-the-pre-crash-status-restarted lifts that to fn-bp-replay-journal, the function host/workflow-host.lisp:8 calls on open: when the replay succeeds, fn-bp-work-status of the installed image is fn-bp-work-status-after-restart of fn-bp-work-status of the trace of the initial state over fn-bp-durable-events, the journal's denotation without that trailing restart. Provenance is separate and also ACL2's: fn-bp-work-origin-at-open-is-recovered-or-absent says that against the id list fn-bp-work-ids records at open, every work the image holds reads :recovered and every other id reads :absent; fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued says this session's durable enqueue of an id that list does not name reads :enqueued. So a work recovered from a cut and a work enqueued after the reopen, which share the status :outstanding, are distinct at the boundary.
proofs.note: Lane w11/workflow-replay, book books/bp-workflow-replay-status.lisp, teeth in tests/acl2/bp-workflow-records-tests.lisp. The subject of the first two keystones is what host/workflow-host.lisp:63 (fn-workflow-work-status) calls; of the last two, what host/workflow-host.lisp:73 (fn-workflow-work-origin) calls on the list host/workflow-host.lisp:8 records. Certified on hbox, run-20260921T005523Z-05dc, build/acl2/certify-20260921T005528Z-1361353. The :enqueue kind hypothesis of fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued has a constructed rather than a reached tooth, and the test book says so: fn-bp-prepare-attempt only prepares an attempt for a work the image holds, so the composed machine reaches no :attempt pending over an image that holds none.

proofs.title: The frame integrity trailer has one owner, and the host's framing is the model's
proofs.statement: fn-frame-trailer (books/frame-trailer.lisp) is the only definition of the 32-octet frame integrity trailer in the tree: it is fn-frame-digest, realised by fn-sha256 through books/crypto-attach.lisp, and it answers :bad rather than a digest for an argument that is not an octet list. For any magic, version, kind and payload in fn-frame-inputp, the byte string a host builds by asking ACL2 for the protected prefix, asking ACL2 for the trailer over it and concatenating the two is fn-frame-seal of those fields; and handing that byte string back to fn-frame-decode with the trailer re-derived over the frame's own fn-frame-protected-prefix answers fn-frame-ok of the fields that went in. The same two statements hold for the store instance the bridge executes, over fn-frame-store-protected and fn-frame-store-decode. Collision and preimage resistance are A-CRYPTO and are not claimed: the attachment introduces no axiom and the seam's constraints are shape only.
proofs.note: Lane w11/one-owner. Keystones fn-frame-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal, fn-frame-decode-of-host-framing and their store instances fn-frame-store-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal and fn-frame-store-decode-of-host-framing, all in books/frame-trailer.lisp. Subject-to-host: the host lines that call fn-frame-trailer are tools/frame_bridge.py FrameSession.trailer (called by seal and digest_of), host/native/io.lisp fnn-trailer (called by fnn-seal and fnn-digest-of) and tools/run_owner.py Acl2Owner.trailer (called by feed_frames and feed_replay_frame); each replaced a separate SHA-256 in that host. Teeth in tests/acl2/frame-trailer-tests.lisp: 25 assert-events, including two FIPS 180-4 vectors, the exact store prefix and trailer octets, the :bad boundary arm, and one violating value per clause (a magic whose third octet is 300 for the shape clause keystone 1 needs, a max-payload of 2 for the bound clause keystone 2 needs, and a non-octet record for the store instance). Byte identity with the deleted host copies was cross-checked outside ACL2 against CPython hashlib.sha256 at 32, 4096, 32768, 262144 and 1048576 octets. NOT closed by this target: fn-frame-digest's collision resistance, and the marshalling cost of sealing a 4 MiB staged inbound bundle through the decimal-octet bridge.
proofs.progress_note: Both books certified with tools/certify_books.py on the laptop (ACL2 8.7, SBCL 2.6.8), evidence dirs above. The four keystones and the 25 assert-events all pass. What the target does NOT establish: collision or preimage resistance of SHA-256 (A-CRYPTO, unchanged by the attachment); and the old tools/run_feed.py driver has since been deleted. W12 feed-durability owns the remaining FNFD envelope/recovery decisions in tools/feed_wire.py and their host adoption; that extension is separate from these trailer theorems.

proofs.title: Prefix and lower-frontier recoverability of a replayed history
proofs.statement: A history that replays successfully leaves an IDLE node whose next txid only moves forward, so dropping its last record leaves a history recoverable at the same frontier, and a history whose txids are all below a bound is recoverable AT that bound. Those are the two facts fn-sf-history-recoverablep needs beyond a successful replay -- together they are fn-replay-advance-okp -- and on them every image the platform may leave in the recovery window is replayable at its own frontier and the host's reopen entry succeeds on it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bytestore-k2, packet 2. fn-sn-replay-loop-append already gave ok(whole) implies ok(prefix); what was missing, and what blocked lane w10/kernel-freedom's first widening at fn-snt-admissible-crash-image-is-recoverable, is that the prefix node is idle with next-txid at most the frontier. The acknowledged-record half of crash-model-v2 K4 is NOT restated over the wider predicate: on both rollback arms the arm's own (null (fn-sf-successes s)) and a member-equal success hypothesis are contradictory, so the restatement would be fn-sn-acknowledged-record-survives-observed-reopen with two vacuous arms. fn-sf-recovery-admissible-image-facts carries that guarantee over every arm instead. Claimed as PRF-033 before merging dev at 81ae082 and RENUMBERED: w11/clock-seam and w11/workflow-replay had taken 033 and 034, and w11/one-owner 035, while this lane held an older dev.

proofs.title: Checkpoint validation refuses a non-journal prefix
proofs.statement: Checkpoint validation binds a checkpoint to exactly one prefix and refuses a prefix that is not an ordered journal interval below the checkpoint frontier: fn-cpc-validp implies the checkpoint is fn-checkpoint-capture-value of that prefix at its frontier, and a prefix with any record whose recorded generation is not its transaction id is refused for every checkpoint and configuration offered with it.
proofs.progress_note: fn-cpc-validp accepted a prefix that fn-checkpoint-capture refuses as :history until 2026-09-21, because fn-replay carries a record generation into the node transitions without comparing it with the txid and validation compared only replay results. The journal-interval clause is now in the recognizer. Open, and not claimed here: fn-cpc-validp has no host caller, so these are properties of a sibling API to the served restore path (host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls fn-checkpoint-restore, which tests the condition itself).

proofs.title: The BPv7 bundle codec inverts, and what fn authors another implementation accepts
proofs.statement: For every bundle satisfying fn-bpb-bundlep whose encoding is within the caller's transfer bound, fn-bpb-decode of fn-bpb-encode is that same bundle and nothing else (fn-bpb-decode-of-encode), resting on the one-block round trip fn-bpb-decode-block-of-encode-block, the fold over the block sequence fn-bpb-decode-blocks-of-encode-blocks and the primary block's half fn-bpb-scan-primary-of-encode; every accepted input yields a bundle (fn-bpb-decode-yields-bundle) and an input over the bound is refused before any octet is examined (fn-bpb-decode-refuses-overlong-input). Over those, the node's two ends: what fn-bpn-send puts on the wire is a bundle (fn-bpn-send-bundle-is-a-bundle), and a peer that accepts what fn-bpn-send authored recovers exactly the ADU that was sent (fn-bpn-receive-of-send-carries-the-adu), under the receiver's own configuration and transfer limit. The covered scope is a whole bundle with at most *fn-bpb-max-blocks* canonical blocks plus the payload block; fragments, BPSec and status reports are outside it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bp-node, 2026-09-21; the codec keystones are lane w10/dtn-3's. All seven named theorems are in books/bp-bundle-invariants.lisp and books/bp-node.lisp, both certified (hbox run-20260921T005707Z-8672 and run-20260921T021131Z-1eb0). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-bundle-tests.lisp and tests/acl2/bp-node-tests.lisp, including the 32-block boundary and the refusal one past it, the three distinct outcomes, and a node configured for a 16-octet transfer refusing a bundle a larger node accepts. The EXTERNAL check is *bpb-dtn7-0-21-0*: 132 octets dtn7-rs 0.21.0 authored, which fn decodes and re-encodes byte for byte (planning/evidence/bp-dtn7-w11-2026-09-21.md). OPEN under this target, and recorded rather than weakened: fn-bpb-decode-blocks-are-canonical-by-construction and fn-bpb-accepted-input-is-canonical-by-construction were REMOVED by w10/dtn-3 after a rewriter runaway with three cures measured and none stopping it, so 'every accepted input re-encodes to itself' is NOT proved for a whole bundle -- it holds of dtn7-rs's captured vector by evaluation only. The native outbound lifecycle now calls fn-bpn-step in books/bp-node-machine.lisp, with source-pinned runtime evidence. This codec target does not cover its persistence, restart or obligation-preservation contracts; PRF-045/046 track those still-open obligations.

proofs.title: Every connection the owner opens carries the operator's AUTHINFO policy, and its greeting says what that policy allows
proofs.statement: fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy: the AUTHINFO configuration pinned into a connection the owner resolved to a peer record (fn-served-open-peer) is the same value pinned into a reader connection opened under that policy (fn-served-open), so no decision in books/nntp-auth.lisp -- the credential fn-auth-authinfo searches, the AUTHINFO and STARTTLS labels fn-auth-capability-lines emits, the 480 gate fn-auth-gatedp applies and the posting allowance fn-auth-postingp computes -- can answer one way for a client the owner resolved as a peer and another way for the client beside it. fn-served-open-peer-pins-the-configuration is the field-level half: the pinned value is the argument, coerced by fn-auth-open-session to fn-auth-open-config only when it is not a configuration. Covered scope: the OPEN transition of one connection; what happens to the policy afterwards is fn-auth-step-preserves-consistent-session's and OB-AUTH-FOLD's. The subject is what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer calls through fn-own-open-peer, which tools/run_owner.py Owner.accept_nntp calls for every accepted socket whose source address matches a peer record. Second half, the same value read where a client first sees it: fn-served-open-greets-200-exactly-when-the-connection-may-post says the greeting the open emits is RFC 3977 section 5.1.2's 200 exactly when the pinned injection configuration allows posting AND fn-auth-postingp of the session just built is true -- which is the conjunction fn-auth-command hands fn-nntp-capability-lines for the POST label and the one fn-auth-postingp decides 340 against 440 and 480 by. fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label states that over the octets a client sees, and is named for what it is: a corollary of the keystone and a local unfold of fn-auth-capability-lines, doing no work of its own. Covered scope: the OPEN transition. It says nothing about the greeting a connection would deserve LATER, after a 281 changes the allowance; RFC 4643 section 2.2 sends the client back to CAPABILITIES for that, and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated is the only statement fn has about the block after a login.
proofs.note: Lane w11/auth-live, decided by measurement and not by inspection. fn-served-open-peer pinned the literal (fn-auth-open-config) while fn-served-open pinned the operator's, and the owner resolves a connection to a peer by SOURCE ADDRESS alone, so on a box where a configured peer is reachable on loopback every client was opened without the operator's policy: AUTHINFO PASS answered 481 with the secret just written, CAPABILITIES carried no AUTHINFO line and POST was never gated. Both theorems are FALSE of that definition. The live before/after is planning/evidence/auth-live-2026-09-21.md and the boundary test is tests/test_auth.py ServedCredentialTests, which starts the node with `bin/fn run` over an fn.toml and writes the peer record, because no test that starts tools/run_owner.py directly can reach this. The greeting half is a second defect the same measurement found: fn-served-greeting read the injection configuration alone, so a connection under [auth] required = true greeted 200 and then answered POST 480, where section 5.1.2's MUST is 201. It takes the opened session now.
proofs.native_scope: The native startup receiver installs the ACL2-produced bounded credential profile before bind, with policy projection and live login evidence. Native configured-peer/source admission and protected transport remain separate; this does not extend the OPEN theorem to every subsequent connection transition.

proofs.title: A host fault costs one connection, and the fourth outcome says so
proofs.statement: fn-own-fault (books/owner-fault.lisp) is the owner's host-fault transition. For any owner and any connection id: the faulted connection is no longer found; every connection with a different id is EQUAL to what it was, so every later step over it has the same input it would have had; a submission in flight for the faulted id, and a pending transaction held by it, are cleared, with no hypothesis that the connection was still open, while a submission in flight for a DIFFERENT id is untouched; the store, the committed view and the completion ledger are unchanged; and the octets the faulted connection receives are RFC 3977 section 3.2.1's 403 and are not the reply octets of fn-nntp-post-outcome for any session and any completion, including that function's own malformed-session 403 -- so the fault is a fourth outcome, distinguishable on the wire from accepted, refused and uncertain.
proofs.note: Lane w11/owner-survival. CLAIMED as PRF-035 and renumbered to PRF-040 on merging dev: 035 had already gone to w11/one-owner's frame trailer, 036 to w11/bytestore-k2, 037 to w11/checkpoint-validator, 038 to w11/bp-node and 039 to w11/auth-live, all inside one evening. Keystones fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection, fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and fn-own-fault-reply-is-not-a-post-outcome (books/owner-fault.lisp), with fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission, fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction and fn-own-fault-is-not-a-store-event beside them. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp on the same witness the served POST scenario builds (*own-taken*: connection 4's submission in flight, reader 3 open), including one violating value per hypothesis and the relation holding after a fault. The host side is tests/test_owner.py OwnerSurvivesAFaultTests, which injects an unexpected exception on one connection and asserts the other is still served. OPEN under this target: nothing states that the HOST calls fn-own-fault at every point where it can fault -- the boundary's coverage is a code property, not a theorem -- and tools/run_reader.py has no such boundary at all. Native host calls fn-owner-fault through fnn-owner-serialized/fault-service, but at checkpoint 76901c1 also stops the service for unexpected serious conditions. The logical single-connection theorem does not establish native service survival; that actual-host obligation remains open. Shared-core failure and uncertain persistence require a global fence and are not justified as connection-local faults by this theorem.

proofs.title: Every byte-level crash image of a related store scans, and scans to an image the file kernel admits
proofs.statement: fn-bs-store-crash-image-scans (K1): for every byte store related to a file-kernel state and every image fn-bs-crash-imagep admits of it, the scan tools/run_store.py performs at open -- the config entry and its integrity check, the frontier entry and its decode, the contiguity of the transaction namespace, and the record list -- returns :ok and not any of its four :fault values. No trailer assumption is used: an authority inode is fenced before any name points at it (D1) and is never overwritten (D2), so the only freedom a crash has over the authority namespace is whether the last entry operation landed. fn-bs-store-crash-image-is-kernel-admissible (K2): what that scan reads is an image fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits, which outside the recovery window is the reliance predicate fn-sf-crash-imagep and inside it is that plus the two rollback arms of D14-b and D14-c -- the record the replay read and has not re-fenced, and the allocator rename that the fourth recovery barrier has not drained. fn-bs-store-recovery-is-a-kernel-crash (K3): fn-sf-image-crash at that image reproduces its frontier, its record list and the :replaying phase. fn-bs-crash-image-reopens: the host reopen entry fn-sn-open-observed succeeds on every such image, in both windows. fn-bs-acknowledged-record-survives-byte-crash (K4): an outcome the store acknowledged before the crash names a record of the state the host reopens on.
proofs.note: Lane w11/k1-scan. CLAIMED as PRF-040 and renumbered to PRF-041 on merging dev: w11/owner-survival had claimed 035, been renumbered to 040 by its own merge, and landed first. That is the fifth collision in two evenings and the board CLAIM line is what caught it here. K1's namespace clause was closed by w9/storage-3; this target closes its other three and everything that waited on them. Books books/byte-store-scan.lisp (K1, K2) and books/byte-store-keystones.lisp (K3, K4, at the seam where the host reopen entry lives), teeth in tests/acl2/byte-store-scan-tests.lisp. The subject of K4 and of fn-bs-crash-image-reopens is fn-sn-open-observed, which host/store-node-host.lisp:70 calls at every process start, reached from tools/run_store.py:1245 (acl2.recover). SCOPE, stated because it is not visible in the statement: K4's instances inside the recovery window are vacuous, because fn-bs-replay-matches-scan carries (equal (fn-sf-successes ks) nil) there and K4's fourth hypothesis is a member of that list; its live instances are the publish window, and what covers the recovery window is fn-bs-crash-image-reopens, which carries no success hypothesis. A positive GROUND witness for K1 does not exist in this tree and the test book says so: an assert-event evaluates and three of the scan's tests are calls of constrained functions (fn-bs-config-okp, fn-bs-frontier-decode, fn-bs-txn-name), so the teeth are the two violating values, one per hypothesis, reached through the scan's first test. Packet P4, which makes the config and frontier files fn-frame frames, is what makes a positive ground witness possible. K0 (fn-bs-program-step-preserves-relation) is still open and is what discharges the relation's own clauses on the host's programs. A later focused K7 packet proves issued record-link and allocator-rename errors, and both authority-directory barrier errors, enter the recovery fence at the exact fn-sn-io subject; K5, K6, K8, general K0 and physical every-cut correspondence remain open, and the exact-octet SIGKILL scenario awaits a frozen developer image.

proofs.title: The inbound transit decision the served path reaches is the model's, over the node the owner holds now (K2 loop, K3 duplicate)
proofs.statement: fn-peer-loop-is-refused: an article whose Path already names this node's path-identity is never accepted through transit, and fn-peer-transfer leaves the node. fn-peer-history-is-have-at-offer and fn-peer-history-is-refused-at-transfer: a Message-ID in the history is :have :history at the offer and is never accepted at the transfer. The subject rule (AGENTS.md rule 1) is closed in two halves: fn-peer-ihave-of-a-held-message-id-is-435-and-no-article and fn-peer-check-of-a-held-message-id-is-438-and-no-offer-outstanding say the reply octets fn-peer-command emits ARE that decision and that the connection does not enter article mode, and fn-own-read-offers-against-the-live-node says the node the served path supplies is fn-sn-node of the owner's own store. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read for the offer, and host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide -> fn-peer-decide-transfer for the transfer. Covered scope: one connection's offer and one article's transfer against one node and one pinned peer record; the hypotheses are the connection facts the decision needs before it reaches its history arm. NOT covered: the peer record is still the one the connection opened with, so a (:set-peer ...) delta reaches the transfer decision and not the offer decision; and fn-peer-decide-transfer emits no :date-future or :no-clock, because the tree has no certified RFC 5322 date-time reader.
proofs.progress_note: Certified on persvati (farm run-20260921T033252Z-6ba2, 0 failures over 87 books: books/peer-inbound, books/peer-inbound-invariants, books/owner, books/owner-invariants, books/served, tests/acl2/peer-inbound-tests, tests/acl2/served-tests). Until w11/transit-correct the offer half was unreachable on a live connection: fn-peer-open-session pinned the node at :open and nothing replaced it, so the wire answered 335 and 238 for an article the connection had itself delivered (V0-TRANSIT-DUPLICATE, V0-TRANSIT-CHECK-DUP at 6fb30ca). The loop half was never inert in the model and was inert in the v0 matrix's deployment, which set no path-identity on either node.

proofs.title: Concrete storage naming, fresh initializer image and conditional frontier preservation
proofs.statement: Under successful syscall outcomes, fn-bs-init-program establishes fn-bs-store-relation from fn-bs-initial-inputp. Under a positive write unit, fn-bs-first-frontier-program preserves that relation when fn-bs-initial-inputp and fn-bs-frontier-inputp hold. The actual fn-bs-step interpreter preserves a related prestate through the enumerated noncommit frontier observations; for a successful directory observation it additionally requires phase :frontier-attempted and independently durable candidate bytes with a quiet root. These are conditional model results: current Store.initialize and Store.advance_frontier correspondence, full initialization/recovery syscall composition, general crash-image preservation, and platform durability remain open. For naturals i and j, equal fn-bs-txn-name-impl outputs imply equal inputs; the constrained naming seam is attached to that renderer. From an empty byte store and initial kernel with fn-bsi-fresh-inputp and successful syscall observations, fn-bsi-current-init-program reaches fn-bsi-current-initial-image, including configuration history and lock publication.
